newsitem.title: GERMANY: German deputy says he was informal Iran mediator.
newsitem.headline: German deputy says he was informal Iran mediator.

text.p: A prominent German politician said on Thursday he acted as informal mediator during a visit to Iran to help improve ties with Bonn, which have been badly damaged by a court ruling that Tehran ordered political killings.

Juergen Moellemann, a parliamentary deputy with the Free Democrats and regarded as a maverick in Bonn, was sharply criticised by Iran's exiled resistance movement as well as deputies from other political parties in Bonn over the visit to Tehran during which he met senior government officials.
But in an interview with Reuters, Moellemann defended the trip saying that although he had not been on a ministry assignment, such contacts could help to boost flagging relations with Bonn.

He said he had notified the German government he planned to accept a "long-standing" invitation from Tehran. He was then briefed by German government officials before the trip and reported his impressions back to Bonn on his return.
"I wanted to talk to several relevant (Iranian) officials to find a way of getting out of a rather difficult situation in a constructive way," said Moelleman, a former economics minister.

"Relations really are at a low ebb at the moment, you can't deny it. We should take advantage of the accession of the new president (Mohammad Khatami) as a chance for new impulses on both sides," said Moellemann.
"Everything Khatami says seems to me to be a good basis for both ties with Germany and Europe," he said, adding that he had met Khatami during the weekend visit.

The National Council of Resistance (NCR) of Iran, which opposes the Tehran government, denounced Moellemann this week, saying his actions condoned Iran's "terrorism abroad" and "suppression at home" and flouted EU policy on Iran.

Bonn deputies from the environmentalist Greens and conservative Christian Social Union (CSU) also criticised him for his "self-appointed mission". The Foreign Ministry in Bonn confirmed he had informed them of his plans but declined comment on the results of his trip.
Iran's state news agency IRNA reported earlier that Moellemann had conveyed a message to Iranian officials from German government officials but did not give further details.

Moellemann said his trip was to hold informal talks with officials, gather impressions of the Islamic Republic after last month's presidential election and continue his personal dialogue with Iranian officials.
He said an improvement in relations was needed after a German court concluded in April that Iran's top leaders had ordered the 1992 assassination of a Kurdish-Iranian dissident in Berlin.
"Ties have not been severed. I'm not talking about a restoration of ties. We need a regeneration in relations," he said, in response to Iranian reports he had called for a restoration of ties.

"I presented the German position on important issues. I was not there for the government but I talked over the trip carefully with government officials before and afterwards to avoid any contradictions," said Moelleman.
Moellemann said he had handed his report on the trip to Chancellor Helmut Kohl and Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel.
European Union (EU) states except for Greece recalled their ambassadors from Tehran after the Berlin court ruling. Iran has repeatedly denied involvement in the killings.
While the EU later agreed the ambassadors could return to Tehran, the bloc has suspended ministerial ties as well as its policy of "critical dialogue" with Iran.
Iranian officials have said the German ambassador would not be welcomed back in Tehran for the time being.
